marker.identification: manual: open markers (no fill), so each seed is the bounding box centre of the orange open triangle found from its colour mask in a 32 px column at each nominal slope; where the circle and the triangle overlap, the visible arc or edges fix the box because marker size is constant (circle 33 px, triangle 35 px tall)

meta.source_title: The Archimede Rover: A Comparison between Simulations and Experiments (Caruso, Giberna, Gorner, Gallina, Seriani; Robotics 12(5), 125, 2023)
meta.x_name: slope angle of the tilted sandbox (nominal, 5 deg steps)
meta.y_name: slip s (median of all drive tests at that slope and wheel speed)
meta.vehicle: Archimede rover prototype, four independently steered and driven wheels, wheelbase 0.720 m, track 0.443 m, body 1.61 kg plus two legs of 1.58 kg (Table 1); commanded mean wheel speed 2.4 rad/s
meta.soil: granular lava, grain size 1 to 5 mm (Test Setup A)
meta.preparation: Planetary Exploration Laboratory sandbox with a tilting section, slope raised in 5 deg steps to 20 deg; drives in straight, lateral and parallel modes pooled; rover tracked by an optical tracking system
meta.comparability_note: Each point is the median slip of all drive tests at that slope and wheel speed, pooling straight, lateral and parallel driving modes (Sec. 3.1.2, 4.2), so not every run is a straight ascent along the fall line. The y axis is labelled s [/] (fraction) although the caption says slip percentage; values are kept as plotted. How s is computed is not written out in Sec. 4.2. Seeds are marker bounding box centres; for the triangles, if the plotting software anchors the marker at the triangle centroid instead, values would be about 0.008 lower. x is the nominal sandbox slope; the actual slope tolerance is not reported. Table 1 prints the wheel diameters as 0.170 and 0.186 with unit mm, which must be metres given the 0.720 m wheelbase; wheel width and grouser height are not reported. load_per_wheel_N derived here from Table 1 masses (1.61 + 1.58 + 1.58 = 4.77 kg) times 9.81 divided by 4 wheels; the table note says the body mass in this work differs slightly. Setup A soil is granular lava of 1 to 5 mm, coarser than dune sand.
